items.title: Steve "Ted" Brown Interview, 1958-04-22
items.q: So I took Eddie around with me and pretty soon Eddie started picking up on his trombone, see?

ctx.x: What pieces did you play then? Do you remember some of the numbers?

We played the same pieces that are played today, only they all have different names. See, we used to call them meatballs and snot, number two. We'd make up a lot of these numbers and we'd just give them a name that way, see? Just joking. And a great many times, one of the fellas would start off and I would ask what he was going to play and he said, well, that's alright, just follow me. So if it sounded good, he'd try to repeat the same thing, you know, then we'd play it different each time, but gradually it would…

Well, it was just about, this tape is just about over now. Yeah, it's just about over. Yeah. I was going to ask, what was number two? What was that tune, I remember? Number two was Tiger Rack. What was the Tiger Rack? And what's the name now of Meatball? I think that was Dixley and Winstead. I don't know what the boys up there gave it.
